title: People disrespect you? This is why.
summary: Forest talk on why kind people get disrespected and abused: most people are neutral and take advantage of perceived weakness, so boundaries only work if you are willing to defend them through conflict. He names three victimization traits (high agreeableness, people pleasing, fear of conflict), traces them to childhood, and prescribes getting comfortable with conflict, saying no, and dropping people who only value you for what you provide.
claims: People who are constantly abused are targeted through predictable strategies, not randomly, and something in them makes it possible
Humans are social but also selfish; most people will take advantage of you when it benefits them, and accepting this early makes life easier
Kind people get abused because they project their own kindness and assume others will respect an unguarded person
Most people are neutral: they are only as good or bad as you allow them to be, and your weakness turns benign people into jerks
Lack of boundaries also ruins potential relationships, friendships and romantic interests, since people lose respect for you
A man who cannot stand up for himself is unattractive to women because he shows he could not stand up for them
Refusing to set boundaries is not niceness but weakness and fear of conflict; it is a pathology, not your identity
A boundary is like a castle wall: useless unless you stand on it and defend it; it is only as strong as your willingness to enforce it
Empty boundaries, like empty threats, teach people your words mean nothing
Avoiding conflict does not make it disappear; it makes you a target and guarantees you lose every confrontation you refuse to enter
As an adult he has had zero fist fights but hundreds of verbal micro-confrontations, which have become more common in modern passive-aggressive society
Boundary-testing is mostly instinctive, as kids show; children without strict boundaries become monsters, and checking them serves them and society
In grad school he took over a shared office and kitchen, leaving dirty dishes and filling the fridge, because nobody checked him
A secretary named Jenny dumped his dirty dishes on his desk; without a word he stopped immediately: pushers only understand defended boundaries
Checking a toxic person protects not just you but everyone around, and even improves the pusher
You choose the people around you; if your circle is toxic it is because you allow it
Predators have a sixth sense for weakness and pick the prey that will not defend itself, which is why victims tend to be revictimized
The three victimization factors are high agreeableness, people pleasing driven by low self-worth, and fear of conflict
These traits usually come from childhood, e.g. a combative parent teaching passivity or a parent giving affection only when you were useful
Abusers deliberately break down self-esteem because self-worth is itself a defense mechanism
Victims are partly responsible because they let abuse happen; just as a country without laws becomes hell, you must build your own police force of boundaries
Failing to do this work leads either to a permanent victim mentality or to becoming jaded and hating humanity
He discarded his own kindness long ago but now thinks that was a mistake; you can keep kindness while defending yourself
Fear of conflict is illogical since others fear it too; when you push back the tester usually backs down, about 98% of the time
When a clearly established boundary is violated, call it out immediately with appropriate severity; attack is the best defense
Flexible, gentle boundaries promoted by some female influencers set women up for abuse; a boundary that is not strict will not be respected
Women need to be twice as severe with boundaries because they lack physical strength to back them up; prefer hurting feelings over danger
He recommends women read The Gift of Fear
Boundary pushers are cowards who stop when called out, and social conventions against violence are what protect them
Think of enforcing a boundary as a jolt of negative social interaction; that alone usually suffices
Defending boundaries builds self-esteem, which makes you more confident so fewer people test you
If verbal checks fail, violence makes you look like the problem; he once punched a persistently tormenting classmate and looked like a psychopath
The usual better option is to cut out people who repeatedly disrespect boundaries, including friends, lovers and family
Children stuck with abusive parents should bide their time and leave when possible rather than resort to violence
Highly agreeable people should gradually build disagreeableness and learn to say no, then stick to it; a retracted no teaches people your words are worthless
People who leave once you start saying no were the ones abusing you; people who appreciate your boundaries are a green flag
You are valuable regardless of how useful you are; test friendships by stopping favours, rides or money and seeing who stays
Kindness chosen from strength has real value, unlike kindness that is a consequence of weakness
